name: Tangier City Beach
notes: Urban bay east of the port; used for kiting in easterly (Levante-type) wind outside the summer crowds.

name: Merkala
notes: Small city beach next to the old harbour; short, fast waves only when a west swell wraps into the Strait in winter.

name: Achakar
notes: Wide Atlantic sand beach south of Cap Spartel; the most consistent surf beach near Tangier and a kite spot in N–W wind.

name: Sidi Kacem
notes: Open sandy beach among dunes next to Achakar; gentle waves on medium NW swell with light easterly wind.

name: Sidi Mghait
notes: Quiet beach south of Asilah with beach-break peaks.

name: Ras Rmel
notes: Larache's ocean beach north of the Loukkos mouth; has hosted national championship qualifying heats.

name: Moulay Bousselham
notes: Exposed beach in front of the village with shifting sandbar peaks; smaller waves in the south corner.

name: Merja Zerga Lagoon Mouth
notes: Inlet of the Merja Zerga lagoon; sandbanks work at low tide and the shallow lagoon offers flat water for kiting.

name: Chlihat
notes: Beach north of the Sebou river jetties near Mehdia, reached by paddling or boat; fast lefts.

name: Mehdia Jetty
notes: Right-hander along the southern Sebou jetty that needs a big NW swell; long walls when it works.

name: Mehdia
notes: Long sand beach south of the Sebou mouth with many beach-break peaks and several surf schools.

name: Plage des Nations
notes: Exposed sandbar beach north of Salé, powerful and uncrowded; summer wind often spoils it.

name: Rabat Beach (Oudayas)
notes: Beach between the Bou Regreg jetties below the Oudayas kasbah; jetty-shaped peaks, the city's learner spot.

name: Harhoura
notes: Beach between Rabat and Temara known locally for its waves.

name: Skhirat
notes: Small left off a jetty near Skhirat that works better at low tide.

name: Oued Cherrat
notes: Rivermouth and beach break with reef rights to the west; one of the most consistent spots of the Rabat–Casablanca coast.

name: Bouznika Beach
notes: Main bay of Bouznika with soft shifting peaks; a learner and longboard beach, busy in summer.

name: Bouznika Point
notes: Long right peeling into the sheltered south end of the bay; rock shelf with urchins.

name: Dahomey
notes: Consistent beach between Bouznika and Mohammedia where many Moroccan surfers learned; summer conditions suit kiters.

name: Les Sablettes
notes: Mohammedia beach with regular, mellow lefts; best in winter.

name: Ain Diab
notes: Casablanca's city beach on the corniche with several peaks and many surf schools; has hosted bodyboard contests.

name: Dar Bouazza
notes: Long left point over urchin-covered reef south of Casablanca; the region's best left and often crowded.

name: Jack Beach
notes: Punchy beach break next to Dar Bouazza; a fallback when other spots are small, with rips in winter.

name: Oued Merzeg
notes: Wide sandy beach at a small river mouth south of Casablanca used by kiters in N–NE wind; rocks at low tide.

name: Azemmour Oum Er-Rbia
notes: Calm water and small waves at the Oum Er-Rbia mouth in strong north wind; long beach downwind to El Jadida.

name: Haouzia
notes: Twelve-kilometre beach north of El Jadida with many peaks; the alternative when Deauville is flat or busy.

name: Deauville
notes: Main El Jadida town beach sheltered by the breakwater; needs NW swell and gets crowded.

name: Sidi Bouzid (El Jadida)
notes: Beach south-west of El Jadida with a fast shorebreak and a point/reef that works with more swell.

name: Oualidia Lagoon
notes: Sheltered lagoon behind the inlet; soft reforming waves for first-timers and flat water for kiting in north wind.

name: La Passe (Oualidia)
notes: Beach break just outside the lagoon mouth with wedging peaks on mid-size NW swell.

name: La Grande Plage (Oualidia)
notes: Long beach along the lagoon with A-frames and wedges off rock stacks.

name: Lalla Fatna
notes: Cliff-backed beach north of Safi with lefts and rights; hosted national championship qualifiers.

name: Sidi Bouzid (Safi)
notes: Beach north of Safi listed for kitesurfing and windsurfing.

name: Safi Garden
notes: World-class right point north of Safi port: long, fast barrels on big NW winter swell.

name: Souiria Kedima
notes: Active beach 36 km south of Safi with water sports; a gentler option than Safi's point.

name: Moulay Bouzerktoun
notes: Windsurf and kite wave spot 25 km north of Essaouira: strong summer north wind and reef waves; World Cup windsurf venue.

name: Essaouira Bay
notes: Town beach sheltered by Mogador island: small waves for learners and the main kite/windsurf school beach in the trade winds.

name: Cap Sim
notes: Fickle right point between Essaouira and Sidi Kaouki, reached by track; for experienced surfers.

name: Sidi Kaouki
notes: Long beach with many sandbar peaks and a reef at the marabout; strong summer wind makes it a wave-kite spot.

name: Tafedna Point
notes: Long right wrapping the cliffs at the north end of Tafedna bay, sheltered from the north wind.

name: Tafedna
notes: Uncrowded village bay with several beach-break peaks.

name: Cathedral
notes: Exposed north side of Imsouane: faster, hollower rights over rock and sand.

name: Imsouane The Bay
notes: Very long, mellow right point in the sheltered bay south of the village; a classic longboard wave.

name: Tamri
notes: Exposed beach with many A-frame peaks north of Cap Ghir; picks up swell when Taghazout is small.

name: Draculas
notes: Fast, hollow right reef near Cap Ghir; experts only.

name: Boilers
notes: Powerful right reef by an old ship's boiler south of Cap Ghir; tricky entry, holds big swell.

name: Imi Ouaddar
notes: Open sandy bay north of Taghazout, best in winter mornings before the wind.

name: Killer Point
notes: Long right point north of Anchor Point that handles big swell; long paddle or a jump off the rocks.

name: La Source
notes: Rock-reef A-frame north of Anchor Point named after a spring on the inside rocks.

name: Mysteries
notes: Short, critical right over rocks just north of Anchor Point.

name: Anchor Point
notes: Morocco's best-known right point at Taghazout, long walls on NW winter swell; WSL Pro Taghazout Bay venue.

name: Hash Point
notes: Mellow right point in front of Taghazout village that needs a decent swell.

name: Panorama
notes: Right point at the south edge of Taghazout, sheltered from wind; beach break at high tide.

name: Taghazout Beach
notes: Beaches south of Taghazout used by surf schools for beginners.

name: K17
notes: Beach break between Taghazout and Tamraght used by surf schools.

name: Devil's Rock
notes: Sandy beach break with A-frames running north from the Tamraght headland; a busy learner spot.

name: Crocodile Beach
notes: Exposed beach next to Devil's Rock with chest-to-head-high A-frames in winter.

name: Banana Point
notes: Right point under the Aourir headland, sheltered from north wind; softer at high tide.

name: Banana Beach
notes: Sheltered beach in front of Banana Village with mushy waves popular with surf camps.

name: K12
notes: Peaks over a rock patch in front of Aourir that behave like a beach break; best on the push.

name: Anza
notes: Beach and reef at Anza north of Agadir port: a right out back and easier inside peaks.

name: Agadir Beach
notes: City beach deep in Agadir bay; needs a big swell and stays small and crumbly.

name: Tifnit
notes: Village bay with soft lefts and right reefs to the north at low tide; hosted national championship heats.

name: Sidi Rbat
notes: Beach with multiple peaks at the Massa estuary, best with light easterly wind in winter.

name: Aglou
notes: Beach of Tiznit; a reef right breaks north of the main beach at Sidi Moussa d'Aglou.

name: Imin Turga
notes: Mirleft's main north-west facing beach with punchy peaks, best on smaller swells.

name: Rasta Point
notes: Right point off the cliff in the middle of Mirleft's main beach, best on the rising tide.

name: Aftas
notes: Small cove below Mirleft village.

name: Marabout Beach
notes: Beach below the Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah shrine with pounding beach breaks between rocks.

name: Tamhrouchte
notes: Long rights wrapping off the northern headland south of Mirleft; the area's best wave but fickle.

name: Sidi El Ouafi
notes: Sheltered beach south of Mirleft with smaller waves and a surf school; rights off the northern rocks.

name: Legzira
notes: Reef right near the red rock arch plus easy beach peaks for surf schools.

name: Sidi Ifni
notes: Town beach with learner shorebreak and a reef right to the north.

name: Teleférico
notes: Powerful left off the ruins of the old Spanish cable-car station; handles large swell.

name: Sidi Ifni Harbour
notes: Beach past the harbour where big NW swell wraps the breakwater into smaller lefts.

name: Plage Blanche
notes: Remote white-sand beach reached by 4x4 south-west of Guelmim.

name: Tarfaya
notes: Windy Cape Juby coast with north-facing beaches picking up NE wind swell.

name: Foum El Oued
notes: Laayoune's beach 25 km from town, known locally as a kitesurf spot in the steady wind.

name: Pointe d'Or
notes: Ocean-side beach and point near the peninsula kite camps, reached by 4x4.

name: Foum Labouir
notes: Large ocean-side bay 5 km from Dakhla with long regular waves off a rocky point; wave kiting in gusty side-shore wind.

name: Lassarga
notes: Sand point at the southern tip of the Dakhla peninsula with a long right; kite and windsurf in the trade winds.

name: Dakhla Lagoon (PK25)
notes: Flat, shallow lagoon water at the PK25 camps; the main beginner and freeride area of Dakhla.

name: Speed Spot
notes: Butter-flat water near Dakhla Attitude with offshore wind; a freestyle and speed spot without on-site rescue.

name: Dune Blanche
notes: Flat turquoise water at the white dune on the lagoon, a classic downwinder destination from the PK25 camps.

name: El Argoub
notes: Lagoon kite area on the south-east shore opposite Dakhla.

name: The Wedge
notes: Right in Taghazout's other central bay between Hash Point and Panorama; needs a fair amount of swell.

name: Imsouane Reef
notes: Hollow rock-bottom wave between The Bay and Cathedral that fires on overhead swell.

name: La Bouteille
notes: Right reef at the north end of Sidi Kaouki beach beside the marabout.
